request.spec:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).
request.prompt:

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A name or alias can no longer be used on a sheet if another sheet in its tree already uses it. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **The tree:** a new `person/TreeNames.java` finds the other sheets in a sheet's tree: its ancestors and all its descendants, counting only sheets that exist. It then collects their names and aliases, ignoring case. Sibling sheets are not part of the tree.
- **What's refused:**
  - **Adding a person** (`BuildPerson`): the name is checked against the tree.
  - **Adding an alias** (`ApplyAlias`): the alias is checked against the tree.
  - **Quick-add** (`FindOrAddPerson`): only when it would create a new person. Adding a claim to someone already on the sheet still works.
  - **Editing a person** (`ApplyPerson`): the new name and the person's existing aliases are all checked. So someone who already clashes can't be edited until the edit gives them a name that doesn't clash, and none of their aliases may clash either.
- **Paste box:** no code change was needed. It only matches people already on the sheet, so a name that isn't there was already refused.
- **Clashing column:** each person now has a `clashing` flag, shown as yes/no in a new "Clashing" column (`person-clashing`). It is always worked out from the tree as it is now, even when you view the sheet as of an earlier date.
- **No database migration:** the flag is calculated when people are loaded, not stored.

**Left unchanged:** transferring a person to another sheet still checks only the target sheet itself, not its tree. The request didn't mention transfers. Also, if the source and target are in the same tree, a tree check would refuse every such transfer unless it skipped the person being moved. Tell me if you want transfers covered too.

Because the new check applies only when something is added or edited, setting a sheet's parent is never refused, even when names already clash. People who already clash are shown as clashing, as the request asks.
